record.question: What type of X-ray beam is used in a multi-slice CT scanner?
record.explanation: Answer A: A cone-shaped beam.. Multislice CT uses a cone-beam geometry spanning multiple detector rows; the source X-ray beam is shaped over a cone rather than a pencil beam. The printed “fan beam” choice better describes single-row CT geometry. Reference: https://www.radiologyinfo.org/en/info/bodyct; https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Contrast-Manual. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
